blocks.title: Atomic orbital
blocks.text: An atomic orbital is the three-dimensional region in space around the nucleus in which the probability of finding the electron is maximum.

The orbitals of each subshell have their own shapes, set by the azimuthal quantum number, and their own orientations, set by the magnetic quantum number. The next three topics describe the s, p, d and f orbitals in turn.

blocks.alt: Six small panels on axes: a small blue sphere for 1s and a larger one for 2s; two cream lobes along the x axis for px and two along the y axis for py; four purple lobes between the axes for dxy, and two lobes on z with a ring for dz2.
blocks.caption: The shapes of s, p and d orbitals drawn flat (original diagram after Figures 2.5b, 2.6 and 2.7).
blocks.long_description: An s orbital is a sphere whose electron density is the same in every direction and which grows with n. A p orbital has two lobes along one axis, and the three p orbitals px, py and pz lie along the three perpendicular axes. The d orbitals have four lobes: dxy, dxz and dyz between the axes of their planes, dx2-y2 along the x and y axes, and dz2 two lobes on the z axis with a doughnut in the xy plane. The seven f orbitals have complicated shapes.
